transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Orion Head of Security), Carlos Duarte (Orion Cloud Eng), Lena Moore (Orion PM)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly security sync touching on SSO setup, audit logs, data retention/PRIVACY, SOC 2 evidence, and an ask to run a short dedicated perf baseline. Agreed next steps around SOC2 docs, SSO metadata exchange, and retention windows.

[00:00] Jamie Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick 30-ish minute sync and then leave time for any deep security Qs, welcome Maya and Carlos and Lena.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Thanks Jamie, yeah we wanted to focus on the security artifacts and a couple items we hit during the pilot, mostly SSO, logs and retention.
[00:20] Riley Chen: Great, I can cover the audit logging hooks and where logs are available in the Private and Dedicated flows, and Jamie will cover documentation and SOC two artifacts.
[00:32] Lena Moore: Quick note — timeline wise the pilot needs to confirm data residency and retention by next week for legal signoff.

[02:10] Carlos Duarte: On SSO we tried the SAML flow last week, got a couple of failures, assertion timeouts and a mismatch on EntityID. Not sure if that was our metadata or the test SP.
[02:25] Riley Chen: Mm hmm, two quick things: our test SAML endpoint expects NameID format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress by default, and the EntityID is case-sensitive. Also our hosted/private control plane exposes a metadata URL — I'll re-share the exact URL and the sample crate of xml.
[02:46] Maya Singh: Perfect — we'll send the metadata. Also curious about support for SCIM for provisioning? We want group sync for roles -> RBAC mapping.
[03:05] Jamie Patel: We do support SCIM for the Redwood Console for Dedicated and Private installs; for Hosted we can enable SCIM for enterprise customers. I'll attach the SCIM endpoints and an example schema in the security pack.

[05:55] Riley Chen: On audit logs — for Dedicated and Private we stream audit events to a customer-controlled destination (S3/GCS or syslog) or we can provide a read-only forwarder; for Hosted we maintain retention by default but we can export full audit trails on request. Logs include token-level metadata, route/model, and request/response hashes — we redact PII from responses unless you opt into full logging for debug.
[06:30] Maya Singh: When you say token-level, do you mean we can see per-request token counts and latency? We need that for cost allocation.
[06:40] Riley Chen: Yes — token counts, latency, model id, route id — all in events. Payloads are hashed by default; full payloads are only exported if explicitly enabled and go into your bucket with KMS encryption.

[08:01] Carlos Duarte: KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption at rest? Bank requirement is keys we control.
[08:12] Jamie Patel: Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated we offer CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) integrated with AWS KMS/HSM. For hosted customers we have a bring-your-own-key option for some enterprise tiers; I'll confirm exact coverage in the pack.
[08:40] Maya Singh: Good. Also want to confirm audit log immutability and WORM-like guarantees for retention windows — legal asks for 7 years for some records.
[08:55] Riley Chen: We can export to your S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled for retention/WORM policies. The control plane also keeps an append-only event stream for the configured retention window; will include details in the docs.

[11:15] Lena Moore: On data residency, we spun up the pilot in us-east-1, but some regulated traffic needs eu-west-1. If we move model traffic regionally will that change SLAs or latency?
[11:30] Riley Chen: Latency will depend on region; our routing policy can pin to region and we can reserve capacity in eu-west-1 via Dedicated capacity to maintain predictable latency. SLA tiers differ by deployment type — Dedicated gives tighter SLOs.

[13:20] Maya Singh: SOC two — we asked for the latest attestation and the list of controls mapped to our internal standards. Do you have that?
[13:30] Jamie Patel: I do — we have SOC 2 Type II (CC) report for our control plane as of 2024 Q4. I'll share the redacted report and a mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks. I'll drop both in the shared folder.
[13:55] Maya Singh: Great — do you also have penetration test results?
[14:05] Jamie Patel: We do periodic pentests; I can provide a summary and an MSA for the scope. Full reports are redacted for public distribution but we can share under NDA or in a secure drop.

[15:40] Carlos Duarte: A nit — during the initial run we saw a few 5xx spikes during long-running sessions, possibly KV cache thrashing or batch timeouts. Could be config on our side but would like Redwood to check.
[15:55] Riley Chen: Yep we saw similar in the logs — likely related to the model seq length and batching window. For the dedicated baseline run I'll tune the batching and prefix caching and run with KV cache warmup to reproduce. I'll attach the perf spreadsheet with parameters.

[18:20] Maya Singh: For the POC we also need a DPA addendum and clarity on data deletion — if a user requests deletion do you purge all derived embeddings and logs? What is the default retention?
[18:35] Jamie Patel: Default retention for hosted is 30 days for request payloads and 90 days for logs; Dedicated/Private are customer-configurable. Deletion requests trigger a purge path — raw payloads and embeddings can be queued for deletion; persistent audit trails (for compliance) can be retained per policy and are exported to your bucket. We'll provide the DPA template.
[19:05] Maya Singh: Need confirmation we can automatically purge embeddings and any cached KV for a user.
[19:15] Riley Chen: Yes, we can invalidate KV cache entries for a tenant and purge embeddings if you opt into that path. For Hosted we need a TTL config; for Dedicated/Private you control retention.

[22:00] Lena Moore: On the topic of role mapping — can we get group-based permissions from SCIM into Console roles?
[22:10] Jamie Patel: Yes, SCIM group sync maps to Console RBAC and you can map groups to roles; we'll attach an example mapping.

[25:30] Maya Singh: A question on breach notification — SLA for notifying customers if their data is accessed?
[25:40] Jamie Patel: We have incident response commitments in the security pack: 72-hour notification for confirmed customer-impacting breaches and a designated contact for critical incidents. For Dedicated/Private we can agree on a faster notification window in the contract addendum.

[28:10] Carlos Duarte: For SSO testing I can share a test IdP file and a test account — Carlos to share.
[28:20] Carlos Duarte: Yep I'll send an exported metadata XML and a test user by end of day tomorrow.

[30:00] Riley Chen: Regarding logs again, note that for Hosted we rotate and encrypt with provider-managed keys; if you want CMEK we can discuss the enterprise path. Also we support streaming to your SIEM via syslog or Kinesis — which one do you prefer?
[30:18] Maya Singh: We prefer Kinesis to integrate with our existing pipeline.
[30:25] Riley Chen: Great, I'll include Kinesis example config for the export connector.

[33:40] Jamie Patel: Next steps recap: I'll share SOC 2 and the security pack (including SCIM/SSO examples, Kinesis/S3 export configs, and DPA). Riley will run the dedicated perf baseline and share the spreadsheet. Carlos will share SAML metadata and test account. Maya will confirm retention windows and legal contact.

[35:00] Lena Moore: Two quick asks: can you also provide a short checklist for our legal team showing which docs they should expect? It speeds up procurement.
[35:12] Jamie Patel: Yes — I'll include a procurement checklist (SOC 2, DPA, ATO/PN, penetration summary, SLA exhibit).

[37:00] Maya Singh: One last thing — tokenization concerns: for embeddings we need to ensure no PII leakage into shared caches. Is there isolation per tenant?
[37:15] Riley Chen: Yes — KV caches and prefix caches are per-tenant in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we use tenant scoping and redaction by default. We'll document the exact guarantees.

[40:00] Carlos Duarte: If we want to move to Dedicated for pilot week 5, what's the lead time?
[40:10] Jamie Patel: Typically 2-3 weeks to provision Dedicated pool depending on capacity and region; I'll confirm availability for eu-west-1 for you.

[42:00] Maya Singh: Sounds good, thanks everyone. We'll expect the docs and the perf run dates.
[42:15] Jamie Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the perf run.
[42:30] Speaker 1: End call.

References / Shared artifacts mentioned:
- Security pack (SOC2, SCIM & SAML examples) — link to share (Jamie to attach)
- Perf spreadsheet — Riley to attach after baseline run
- DPA template and procurement checklist — Jamie to attach

Transcript notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., \"K M S\" for KMS, \"SOC two\" for SOC 2, \"V P C\" for VPC) and occasional speaker label noise.
